question: What is the general shape of a standard intrauterine device?
explanation: Standard intrauterine devices are manufactured in a T-shape so they can fit securely within the anatomical dimensions of the uterine cavity. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h1)

question: Why do many clients prefer intrauterine devices over short-acting methods like oral contraceptive pills?

options.C: They offer immediate protection against sexually transmitted infections
options.D: They can be purchased without any clinical assessment

explanation: Long-acting reversible contraceptives remove the burden of daily or coital-dependent actions, significantly lowering typical-use failure rates. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h1)

question: How do non-hormonal copper intrauterine devices primarily prevent pregnancy?

options.A: By creating a spermicidal inflammatory environment
options.B: By thickening the cervical mucus into a solid barrier
options.C: By completely suppressing the release of ovarian eggs
options.D: By expanding the muscular walls of the fallopian tubes

explanation: Copper ions induce a local biochemical reaction inside the uterus that damages sperm cells and halts their ascent toward the fallopian tubes. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h2)

question: What is a primary local effect of the progestin released by a hormonal IUD?

options.A: Thinning and atrophy of the endometrial lining
options.B: Alkalinization of the normal vaginal pH balance
options.C: Dilation of the internal cervical os structures
options.D: Hypertrophy of the myometrial muscle layers

explanation: The continuous local presence of progestin keeps the endometrium thin, rendering it unsuitable for the implantation of a fertilized ovum. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h2)

question: Which specific copper IUD model is most commonly supplied in Nigerian public health clinics?
explanation: The Copper T 380A is the standard device distributed through government reproductive health programs because of its affordability and long lifespan. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h3)

question: What is a major barrier to the widespread uptake of hormonal IUDs in many resource-constrained Nigerian communities?

options.A: Universal legal bans on hormonal contraception
options.B: Complete lack of trained insertion personnel
options.C: Inability of the devices to withstand tropical heat

explanation: While highly effective, hormonal IUDs are often expensive to purchase privately, making them less accessible compared to subsidized copper alternatives. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h3)

question: Which of the following is an absolute contraindication to inserting an intrauterine device?
explanation: An IUD must never be placed if a woman is pregnant, as it risks severe infection, septic abortion, and excessive hemorrhage. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h4)

question: Why is a bimanual pelvic examination performed immediately prior to an IUD insertion procedure?

options.A: To determine the size and anatomical position of the uterus
options.B: To dilate the cervical os for easier instrument passage
options.C: To clean the vaginal vault of normal physiological flora
options.D: To measure systemic hormone levels via mucosal absorption

explanation: Assessing uterine position (such as anteverted or retroverted) prevents uterine perforation by aligning procedural instruments correctly. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of using a uterine sound before inserting an IUD?

options.A: To stimulate local estrogen production in the endometrium
options.B: To measure the depth and direction of the uterine cavity
options.C: To destroy any bacteria residing within the cervical canal
options.D: To permanently seal the internal os against infection

explanation: Sounding prevents the inserter from pushing past the fundus, which is the leading cause of accidental uterine perforation. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h5)

question: How should a nurse manage routine IUD removal when pulling the threads causes the client unexpected, severe pain and resistance?

options.A: Administer oral analgesics and wait ten minutes before trying again
options.B: Cut the threads flush with the cervix and leave the device inside
options.C: Apply maximum physical force to overcome the cervical resistance
options.D: Stop pulling immediately and investigate for embedding or complications

explanation: Resistance or severe pain during removal suggests the device may be embedded in the myometrium or displaced, requiring specialized evaluation. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h5)

question: What change in menstrual pattern is most commonly reported by users of copper intrauterine devices?

options.A: Unpredictable spotting lasting only one day
options.B: Heavier and more painful menstrual bleeding
options.C: Complete cessation of all monthly cycles
options.D: Total absence of cramping and discomfort

explanation: The local inflammatory reaction caused by copper devices often results in heavier flows and increased cramping, particularly during the first few months. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h6)

question: What guidance should a nurse give a client regarding checking their IUD strings?

options.A: Pull downward on the strings monthly to test device security
options.B: Feel for the strings in the upper vagina after menstrual periods
options.C: Avoid touching the area entirely to prevent accidental expulsion
options.D: Use a mirror and speculum daily to inspect the external os

explanation: Checking strings periodically helps confirm the device remains in place, and doing so after menses is ideal when expulsion risk is slightly higher. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h6)

question: When is a client at the highest risk for developing pelvic inflammatory disease following an IUD insertion?

options.A: Immediately before the next menstrual period
options.B: Only during the final year of device expiration
options.C: Between two and five years after insertion
options.D: Within the first twenty days post-insertion

explanation: Bacterial introduction during the insertion procedure creates a temporary window of vulnerability for upper reproductive tract infections. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h7)

question: A client presents to the clinic complaining that she can no longer feel her IUD strings and is experiencing sharp, persistent pelvic pain. What complication must the nurse suspect first?

options.C: Complete dissolution of the copper frame
options.D: Normal hormonal adaptation to the device

explanation: Missing strings combined with pelvic pain are classic warning signs that the device has either perforated the uterine wall or been expelled. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T015#GNS226_U6_T015_h7)
